definitions.explanation: A stone slab used for grinding solid ink sticks with water to produce liquid ink for calligraphy or painting.

examples.english: To grind ink on an inkstone.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}から{硯|すずり}を{譲|ゆず}り{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I inherited an inkstone from my grandfather.

examples.japanese: {書道|しょどう}には{良|よ}い{硯|すずり}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Good calligraphy requires a quality inkstone.

notes:
CALLIGRAPHY EQUIPMENT:
One of the {文房四宝|ぶんぼうしほう} (Four Treasures of the Study):
- {筆|ふで}: brush
- {墨|すみ}: ink stick
- {硯|すずり}: inkstone
- {紙|かみ}: paper

STRUCTURE:
A {硯|すずり} typically has:
- {陸|おか}/{丘|おか}: the flat grinding surface
- {海|うみ}/{池|いけ}: the depression where the liquid ink collects

QUALITY:
Fine inkstones are prized by calligraphers. Famous varieties include:
- {端渓硯|たんけいけん} from China (Duanxi)
- {雨畑硯|あまはたすずり} from Japan (Yamanashi Prefecture)

USE:
A {墨|すみ} (ink stick) is ground in circular motions on the {硯|すずり} with a small amount of water to produce ink of the desired consistency.
